seriesName: Rex Fleet Academy: Reach and Resolve
format: Academy doctrine/history series told through a recurring seminar cohort, historical case studies, simulations, and occasional field exercises.
storyEngine: Instructor poses a practical doctrine problem; students expose assumptions from different professional and regional backgrounds; a dramatized historical or operational case complicates the easy answer; the class returns to a changed problem rather than a slogan.
canonPrinciples: Reach means restoring contact, trade, rescue capacity, knowledge exchange, and coexistence; it is not synonymous with expansion or Fleet presence.
Resolve means sustaining viable communities, infrastructure, memory, and decision-making when connection fails; it is not synonymous with isolation.
Resolve makes Reach possible; Reach gives Resolve purpose.
The mature problem is balancing both under finite time, capacity, consent, and uncertainty.
Historical sequences must preserve their era: post-Break antecedents may foreshadow later Fleet, Verge, and Shard traditions without importing mature faction design wholesale.

academyCurriculum.planStatus: Issue 1 is the default complete course. The former six-entry issue list is now a candidate-module pool.
academyCurriculum.issueCountPolicy: One issue by default; two or three only if the doctrine/source material needs additional dramatic room. Three is the expected maximum.
academyCurriculum.sourceTextProgram: See academy_source_program.json. Treatise/doctrine excerpts may run as source captions while the seminar and reconstructed case show what the language protects, misses, or later becomes.

productionIssues.title: The Two Failures
productionIssues.premise: The cohort studies the first rescue vessel after the Resolve Circle and two settlements that nearly fail for opposite reasons: Orison through dependence, Varda through isolation.

candidateModules.title: The Cost of Connection
candidateModules.premise: A reopened corridor brings medicine, standards, credit, and traffic to an independent settlement; the class studies when interoperability becomes dependency or political absorption.

candidateModules.title: The Cost of Standing Alone
candidateModules.premise: A community celebrated for self-sufficiency discovers that its closed technical and civic systems have become brittle; the Academy examines when resilience hardens into refusal to learn.

candidateModules.title: The Verge Rule
candidateModules.premise: A Verge logistics case shows a culture that accepts convoys while building local capacity anyway: take the convoy, build the greenhouse, keep the route open, never assume it will remain open.

candidateModules.title: Who Gets to Decide?
candidateModules.premise: A humanitarian crisis forces the cohort to separate local sovereignty from local coercion and outside assistance from outside jurisdiction.

candidateModules.title: A Ship Is a Contradiction
candidateModules.premise: A training cruise becomes a live operational test: a Fleet ship is a self-sufficient piece of civilization using that independence to reconnect others, forcing the cohort to apply Reach and Resolve without a classroom answer.

courseArchitecture.continuationRule: The doctrine cases are candidate modules, not Issues 2–6. If continuation is justified, combine the strongest complementary cases into at most two additional issues.
courseArchitecture.castScope: Professor Talia Merin and this cohort belong to Reach and Resolve only unless another course explicitly reuses them.
courseArchitecture.imgScope: Use a dedicated Reach and Resolve IMG/reference project when visual production begins.
